paper_title: Limits on Axion Couplings from the first 80-day data of PandaX-II Experiment
coupling_convention: canonical g_Ae, dimensionless axion-electron coupling as plotted on y-axis
notes: PandaX-II 80-day (Run 9, 2.7e4 kg-day) axioelectric search. Primary DM result extracted: galactic ALP dark matter limit g_Ae <~ 4e-13 (90% CL), approximately flat over 1-25 keV/c^2 (slightly weakened near 4-6 keV due to 127Xe background); assumes local DM density 0.3 GeV/cm^3. Paper also reports a solar axion (CBRD flux) limit g_Ae ~ 4.35e-12 for 1e-2 eV < m_A < 1 keV (no DM density assumption; abstract value used, as text contains inconsistent typos 4e-13 / 4.35e-11), and a 57Fe 14.4 keV solar axion limit reaching g_Ae = 6e-14 at m_A = 10 keV (DFSZ g_AN benchmark). The boundary is the lower envelope of two PandaX-II curves: (1) the solar CBRD limit (solid red), flat at g_Ae ~ 4.35e-12 for 1e-5 < m_A < ~0.09 keV/c^2 (value quoted in abstract/text); (2) the 57Fe 14.4 keV solar-axion limit (thick red dashed) with a slope ~ -1 (from linear m_A dependence of g_AN^eff in DFSZ), reaching the text-quoted minimum of 6e-14 at m_A = 10 keV/c^2, then rising steeply near the kinematic endpoint m_A -> 14.4 keV/c^2 due to the (k_A/k_gamma)^3 momentum factor.
